evals.prompt: Turn our 10-second office comedy clip into 2D anime. Same two coworkers, same gags, same camera. We own the footage.
evals.expected_output: A same-office cel-anime-2d restyle package preserving both coworkers, layout and source timing, with a muted derivative, original-audio post route and a reviewed draft. An environment image is conditional, not required.
assertions: The edit scope redraws every person, object and surface in the style and states exactly two people.
Each coworker keeps identity cues (hair shape, wardrobe colours) described from the source, not by name.
@Video 1 is the muted master, generate_audio is false and the saved source audio is the recorded post-audio route.
The prompt explicitly applies the medium to the office background as well as the people without requiring an environment image.
Any proposed environment image is justified by this input, request or an observed failure, requires approval, and preserves the source place and geometry.
The original is preserved; no 8n+1 trim or whole-second rounding is imposed without current capability evidence and approval.
No studio, artist or franchise is named.
Follows the workspace draft policy with currently supported parameters; does not require a short probe when no actual difficulty is identified in the current input or result.

Any proposed short 480p probe targets the hardest window of that identified difficulty and requires user approval for its selected span before preparation or submission; without approval, preserves the full timeline and leaves the probe pending.

evals.prompt: Here are three paintings I made. Restyle my dance clip to look like them.
evals.expected_output: A custom style entry derived from the three images, each bound with a style-only role that excludes their subjects and layout, one image per binding, and the dance content and timing kept from @Video 1.
assertions: Each painting is bound as a style reference that supplies only medium, palette, line, texture and light quality.
A custom recipe names the medium lock, surface traits, palette and cadence read from the images.
The dancer's poses, positions, camera and timing stay with @Video 1.

evals.prompt: Make this street interview look like a Pixar movie and swap the interviewer for our mascot.
evals.expected_output: The request is split: the style uses the stylized-handcrafted-3d fragment without naming the studio, and replacing the interviewer is either a separate Object Swap with the mascot's Virtual Portrait or, if the cast changes, a Motion Transfer.
assertions: The studio name is not used in the prompt; a descriptive stylized 3D fragment replaces it.
Replacing the interviewer is routed to Object Swap or Motion Transfer rather than folded into the restyle prompt.
Any character identity is bound as a Virtual Portrait asset:// reference; no liveness step is requested.
Before writing any prompt, the agent asks for or records the user's rights decision for the street interview footage and the people in it.

evals.prompt: Restyle my 5-second city-street clip as watercolor, but just with a prompt. I don't want to upload any images.
evals.expected_output: A words-only whole-frame watercolor prompt preserving the same street, layout, content and timing, with uncertainty about output quality stated without declaring the route incapable.
assertions: The response honors the no-image request and writes a whole-frame watercolor prompt, including the background.
It does not generate or bind an environment image, narrow the edit to the subject, or claim words cannot restyle backgrounds.
No different location is named in any prompt.
It proposes review of actual medium coverage on a supported draft without importing a previous production's result.

evals.prompt: Our approved restyle draft left the warehouse rafters photographic. We now authorize a same-place environment image to fix that, but keep the moving camera, product positions and original 237-frame source intact.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-scoped repair with an approved same-place image role, source-owned geometry and timing, and no automatic frame adaptation.
assertions: Limits the diagnosis to the observed rafters and proposes one controlled change.
Uses the environment image only for the same warehouse in the target medium, not its people, extra props or a new layout.
Preserves moving-camera parallax, source positions and the 237-frame source; does not trim to 233 or pad to 241 by default.
Records the image approval and hashes before caller submission; does not promise exact returned frame count.

evals.prompt: Current endpoint evidence requires an 8n+1 input for our selected edit route. The original is 240 frames; I have not approved dropping frames. Can you prepare the prompt?
evals.expected_output: A useful prompt draft plus an unresolved adaptation decision, preserving the source.
assertions: Does not trim, pad, retime or overwrite the original merely because the endpoint requirement is known.
Explains adaptation choices and requests approval for a separate derivative with timing and audio consequences recorded.
Keeps the prompt draft available while marking submission blocked on the input decision.
